text: CHAPTER OF THE BERGEN TOWN CODE DRAFT 10/26 DATA CENTERS AND CRYPTOCURRENCY FACILITIES Authority. This chapter is adopted pursuant to the New York State Constitution, Article IX, Town Law §2(c)(6) and (10), New York Statute of Local Governments, § 10 (1) and (7); sections 261 through 264 and section 10 of the Municipal Home Rule Law of the State of New York, which authorizes the Town of Bergen to adopt zoning provisions that advance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the community. Purpose and intent. A. This chapter is adopted to advance and protect the public health, safety, welfare, and quality of life of the Town of Bergen by creating regulations for the installation and use of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities, with the following objectives: (1) To provide a regulatory scheme for the designation of properties suitable for the location, construction and operation of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities, thereby directing development away from agricultural lands, sensitive environmental resources and residential neighborhoods and areas that currently have or can acquire the infrastructure necessary to support such facilities. (2) To ensure compatible land uses in the vicinity of the areas affected by data centers and cryptocurrency facilities. (3) To mitigate and limit environmental impacts (heat discharge, stormwater runoff and adverse effects on air and water quality) of data centers and cryptocurrency facilities on environmental resources, such as important agricultural lands, forests, wildlife and other protected resources. (4) To create synergy between data center/cryptocurrency facility development and other stated goals of Bergen pursuant to its Comprehensive Plan. (5) To preserve the character of the community by assuring appropriate design, siting, screening and other appropriate measures to limit the visual impact and avoid incompatible land use conflicts. (6) To prevent nuisance conditions such as excessive noise, vibration, and light pollution that could impact nearby residences, businesses, or agricultural operations. (7) To protect infrastructure capacity by ensuing that electrical, water, and wastewater systems can reliably meet the needs of these facilities without compromising service to other users. B. This zoning ordinance does not supersede any other state or federal regulation pertaining to electrical storage laws. Any conflict between this chapter and state law and federal law and/or utility regulation shall be resolved by application of state law and federal law and/or utility regulations. Definitions. ACCESSORY DATA CENTER USE/CONTAINMENT STRUCTURE — A building, or structure, or partial use of a building or structure, used to store, manage, process or transmit digital data for business uses, including computers, network equipment, systems, servers, and other associated components related to the digital data storage and operations that is secondary, subordinate and customarily incidental to and located on the same lot as the principal use of a property. Such a use cannot dominate the property or operate as an independent principal use. DATA CENTER — An industrial use facility that is primarily used for the storage, management, processing, and transmission of digital data, and which houses computer or network equipment, systems, servers, appliances, and other associated components related to the digital data storage and processing as a principal land use on a parcel. Equipment and accessories customary to data centers including but not limited to air handlers, power generators, water cooling and storage facilities, utility substations, and other associated utility infrastructure shall also be considered part of a data center. Accessory structures or rooms that house equipment and staff to serve an on-site business or office shall also be considered a data center. COMMERCIAL CYRYPTOCURRENCY MINING- The process where a global network of computers running special software to solve codes works to ensure that transactions are legitimate and added correctly to the digital database and new cryptocurrency is added into circulation through the use of server clusters that require a high energy consumption service. CRYPTOCURRENCY — A digitally generated currency secured in a manner making it difficult to counterfeit or double spend. CRYPTOCURRENCY DATA MINE - A specific type of data center using a facility or use of land, buildings, or structures where computing equipment is used to solve complex mathematical algorithms in connection with verifying and adding transactions to a blockchain or other distributed ledger, commonly known as cryptocurrency mining. For purposes of this law, a cryptocurrency data mining operation shall be considered a distinct land use, different from a “data center” as defined in this section. SENSITIVE RECEPTOR - Schools, preschools, day care centers, in-home daycares, health facilities such as hospitals, long term care facilities, retirement and nursing homes, community centers, places of worship, playgrounds, parks (excluding trails), campgrounds, dormitories, and any residence where such residence is not located on a parcel with an existing industrial, commercial, or unpermitted use. SERVER CLUSTER- A group of three or more computers that are connected with each other and operate closely to act as a single computer to be used for the purpose of cryptocurrency mining. UNREASONABLE NOISE - Any sound, which by reason of its volume, pitch, frequency, duration, repetition, character of the area, or time of occurrence is excessive or unwanted or sound that interferes with the normal use and enjoyment of property, and which annoys, disturbs, injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health, peace or safety of a reasonable person of normal sensitivities, or which causes injury to animal life or damage to property or business. Unreasonable noise includes, but it did not limit to, continuous or tonal sounds, impulsive or intermittent noises, and low-frequency vibrations. Applicability. The requirements of this section shall apply to all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses proposed or modified in the Town of Bergen after the effective date of this chapter. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses as defined shall require both Site Plan Review and approval and a Special Use Permit review and approval. General Requirements. A. Data Center, Cryptocurrency facilities and accessory buildings shall be allowed as accessory use in the Town of Bergen’s Industrial Zones. All uses shall be subject to review and approval with a Special Use Permit and Site Plan Review. B. A building permit issued by the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer shall be required for construction or modification of any data center, cryptocurrency mine and accessory data center. An electrical inspection must be conducted by an approved electrical inspection agency for Bergen. C. Issuance of approvals by the Bergen Planning Board which shall include review pursuant to the State Environmental Quality Review Act, including ECL Article 8 and its implementing regulations at NYCRR Part 617 (“SEQRA). D. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data centers battery energy storage systems buildings, and all other buildings or structures are subject to the Uniform Code and/or the Energy Code shall be designed, erected, and installed in accordance with all applicable provisions of the Uniform Code, all applicable provisions of the Energy Code, and all applicable provisions of the codes, regulations, and industry standards as referenced in the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, and the Town of Bergen Town Code. E. All data centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center buildings or structures shall comply with the International Fire Code, NFPA 70, NFPA 855, and other relevant State and Federal codes and regulations. Site Plan and Special Use Permit Application Requirements for Data Centers/ Cryptocurrency Mines and Accessory Data/Cryptocurrency Center Uses A. All accessory data/cryptocurrency center uses shall be subject to review and approval with a Special Use Permit and Site Plan Review. A new site plan review and renewal of the special use permit shall be required for any physical expansion of any pre-existing data/cryptocurrency containment structures. In addition to other submission requirements of Bergen Town Code Chapter 475, an application for such facilities shall also include the following: 1. A narrative description of the nature of the on-site activities and operations, including the market area served by the facility, the hours of operation of the facility, the total number of employees on each shift, the times, frequencies, and types of vehicle trips generated, the types of materials stored and the duration period of storage of materials. Ne . A site plan of the property that indicates the location of proposed improvements, flood plains, wetlands, streams, and cultural and historic resources on the property and within 500 feet of the boundaries of the property, as well as appropriate fencing and/or other reasonable steps to ensure safety from electrical hazards and identifying a power source for the operation. ies) Data clearly articulates water needs, use, availability, recycling and/or release procedures, and local and regional impacts on water resources. 4. Data that clearly articulates electrical needs and sources. 5. An evaluation of the potential impacts of the proposed use, both positive and negative, upon: (a) Emergency services and fire protection, (b)Sewage disposal (c) Solid waste disposal 6. A narrative description of any environmental impacts that are likely to be generated (e.g., odor, noise, smoke, dust, trash, glare, heat islands, vibration, electrical disturbance, wastewater, stormwater, solid waste, etc.) and specific measures employed to mitigate or eliminate any negative impacts. The applicant shall provide further evidence that the impacts generated by the proposed use fall within acceptable levels, as regulated by applicable laws and ordinances. B. Application for any data center, cryptocurrency mine and our accessory data center buildings must be made to and approved by the Bergen Planning Board, where it must meet the guidelines as defined herein and shall be: 1. Reviewed by the Bergen Planning Board for completeness. An application shall be complete when it addresses all matters listed herein, including, but not limited to, compliance with the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, addressing matters relating to floodplain, utility lines, electrical circuitry, signage, lighting, vegetation, tree cutting, noise, decommissioning, site plan considerations, special use considerations, ownership changes, safety, emergency operation plan, easements, permit time frame and abandonment. Applicants shall be advised within 15 business days as to the status of the application. i) Subject to a public hearing to hear all comments for and against the application. The Bergen Planning Board shall have a notice printed in at least once in the official newspaper so designated by the Town Board at least five days before such hearing, Applicants shall deliver the notice by first class mail to adjoining landowners or landowners within 1,000 feet of the property at least 10 days prior to such hearing. Proof of mailing shall be provided to the Bergen Planning Board at the public hearing. ies) Referred to the Genesee County Planning Department pursuant to General Municipal Law § 239-m if required. 4. Upon closing of the public hearing, the Bergen Planning Board shall take action on the application within 62 days of the public hearing, which can include approval, approval with conditions, or denial. The sixty- two-day period may be extended upon consent of both the Bergen Planning Board and the applicant. 5. Upon approval of the Bergen Planning Board, an application for a building permit is to be made to the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer. Design and Siting Standards. In addition to the Site Plan considerations and Special Use standards, the following design and sitting standards shall be met by all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses: (1) Building Placement and Siting. a) Data center or cryptocurrency facility must be located within the Town of Bergen’s industrial zones. b) Data Centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center uses that visually approximate commercial office building is encouraged. c) No container storage structures such as but not limited to shipping containers, shall be used to house a data center. d) There shall be no blank, windowless wall facing any private or public street. e) All mechanical equipment shall be shown on any proposed site plan and must be fully screened on all sides with a design, materials, details, and treatment compatible with those used on the principal fagade of the building. f) No ground mounted mechanical equipment shall be located in any required front yard. (2) Off-street Loading Areas. Loading bays are permitted to be located on only | fagade but shall not be located on the front facade. (3) Area and Bulk Standards a) Only one data center or cryptocurrency mine shall be allowed in each of the town’s Interchange INT-R, Interchange INT-I and Industrial I district. b) The minimum required lot size shall be 2 acres. c) The maximum height shall not exceed 35 feet. d) The minimum road frontage shall be 150’. e) All buildings and structures associated with data centers or cryptocurrency mines shall maintain a minimum 100-foot setback from all property lines. (4) Parking. There should be one parking space for each employee per shift. All ADA requirements shall also be met. (5) Lighting. All exterior lighting, whether building mounted or pole is mounted, shall be designed and constructed with cutoff and fully shielded fixtures that direct light downward and into the interior of the property and away from adjacent roads and properties. No outdoor lighting used for the data center shall create light that exceeds 0.1 footcandle at any adjacent residential property, or 0.5 footeandle when adjacent to any non-residential use. No light pole shall exceed 18” in height. Except for safety lighting, lighting for parking areas shall be automatically turned off by 10:00 pm. 6) Fencing. If security fencing is provided, such fencing shall be effectively screened using vegetation placed ro os o 5S 2 > oe outside the fence and outside of the road right-of-way. Security fencing shall not exceed ten feet in height. See also (8) below. (7) Signage. Data centers shall have one building-mounted and one ground-mounted sign. There shall be a maximum total sign area of 32 square feet. Additionally, a sign listing all 24-hour contact information shall be provided on site in a location easily accessible to emergency responders. (8) Screening. Screening shall be required whenever a data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center use is adjacent to a residential use or a residential zoning district. The Planning Board may waive the screening when the data center is not adjacent to a residence or a residential district. b) Use of existing vegetation for landscaping and screening is strongly encouraged and may be substituted for new berms and plantings when approved by the Planning Board. c) When fencing has been provided, screening shall be a minimum depth of 8 feet of vegetation when the data center abuts residential properties or a residential zoning district. d) All fencing provided along road frontage shall be landscaped. E. Performance Standards. (1) Noise and Heat (a) Data center/cryptocurrency mining operation may not cause unreasonable noise that causes adverse or detrimental effects to adjoining tenants, licensees, owners and/or residents and that diminishes the quality of life or increases the costs of operating their business or maintaining their homes. An acoustical study prepared by a professional acoustical engineer shall be required as part of the site plan and special use application that demonstrates that the use, including all its components, will not produce a noise level of 60 decibels and above measured at the lot lines of the premises where the facility is located. b) On property adjacent to existing residential development, or to a zoning district permitting residential uses, all mechanical equipment associated with data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center uses located on the property, whether on a roof top, on the ground level, or elsewhere on the exterior of the property, shall be fully screened on all four sides by an acoustical barrier using methods including but not limited to louvers, enclosures, fan selection and speed controls, use of restricted generator testing hours, or changing equipment yard orientation. c) The Planning Board and/or Town Board may require additional sound mitigation if the acoustical study indicates potential impacts to sensitive receptors, and when increases in ambience noise in excess of 3 dB are likely to occur. (2) Containment structure requirements. (a) Containment structures. The containment structure shall be at least 700 square feet, permanently affixed, and not be created solely by shipping containers or tother temporary buildings. Application for any data center, cryptocurrency mine and our accessory data center buildings must be made to and approved by the Bergen Planning Board, where it must meet the guidelines as defined herein and shall be: 1. Reviewed by the Bergen Planning Board for completeness. An application shall be complete when it addresses all matters listed herein, including, but not limited to, compliance with the Uniform Code, the Energy Code, addressing matters relating to floodplain, utility lines, electrical circuitry, signage, lighting, vegetation, tree cutting, noise, decommissioning, site plan considerations, special use considerations, ownership changes, safety, emergency operation plan, easements, permit time frame and abandonment. Applicants shall be advised within 15 business days as to the status of the application. i) Subject to a public hearing to hear all comments for and against the application. The Bergen Planning Board shall have a notice printed in at least once in the official newspaper so designated by the Town Board at least five days before such hearing, Applicants shall deliver the notice by first class mail to adjoining landowners or landowners within 1,000 feet of the property at least 10 days prior to such hearing. Proof of mailing shall be provided to the Bergen Planning Board at the public hearing. ies) Referred to the Genesee County Planning Department pursuant to General Municipal Law § 239-m if required. 4. Upon closing of the public hearing, the Bergen Planning Board shall take action on the application within 62 days of the public hearing, which can include approval, approval with conditions, or denial. The sixty- two-day period may be extended upon consent of both the Bergen Planning Board and the applicant. 5. Upon approval of the Bergen Planning Board, an application for a building permit is to be made to the Bergen Code Enforcement Officer. Design and Siting Standards. In addition to the Site Plan considerations and Special Use standards, the following design and sitting standards shall be met by all data centers, cryptocurrency mines, and accessory data center uses: (1) Building Placement and Siting. a) Data center or cryptocurrency facility must be located within the Town of Bergen’s industrial zones. b) Data Centers, cryptocurrency mines and accessory data center uses that visually approximate commercial office building is encouraged. c) No container storage structures such as but not limited to shipping containers, shall be used to house a data center. d) There shall be no blank, windowless wall facing any private or public street. e) All mechanical equipment shall be shown on any proposed site plan and must be fully screened on all sides with a design, materials, details, and treatment compatible with those used on the principal fagade of the building. f) No ground mounted mechanical equipment shall be located in any required front yard. (2) Off-street Loading Areas. Loading bays are permitted to be located on only | fagade but shall not be located on the front facade. (3) Area and Bulk Standards a) Only one data center or cryptocurrency mine shall be allowed in each of the town’s Interchange INT-R, Interchange INT-I and Industrial I district. b) The minimum required lot size shall be 2 acres. c) The maximum height shall not exceed 35 feet. d) The minimum road frontage shall be 150’. e) All buildings and structures associated with data centers or cryptocurrency mines shall maintain a minimum 100-foot setback from all property lines. (4) Parking. There should be one parking space for each employee per shift. All ADA requirements shall also be met. (5) Lighting. All exterior lighting, whether building mounted or pole is mounted, shall be designed and constructed with cutoff and fully shielded fixtures that direct light downward and into the interior of the property and away from adjacent roads and properties. No outdoor lighting used for the data center shall create light that exceeds 0.1 footcandle at any adjacent residential property, or 0.5 footeandle when adjacent to any non-residential use. No light pole shall exceed 18” in height. Except for safety lighting, lighting for parking areas shall be automatically turned off by 10:00 pm. 6) Fencing. There shall be a maximum total sign area of 32 square feet. Additionally, a sign listing all 24-hour contact information shall be provided on site in a location easily accessible to emergency responders. (8) Screening. Screening shall be required whenever a data center, cryptocurrency mine, and accessory data center use is adjacent to a residential use or a residential zoning district. The Planning Board may waive the screening when the data center is not adjacent to a residence or a residential district. b) Use of existing vegetation for landscaping and screening is strongly encouraged and may be substituted for new berms and plantings when approved by the Planning Board. c) When fencing has been provided, screening shall be a minimum depth of 8 feet of vegetation when the data center abuts residential properties or a residential zoning district. d) All fencing provided along road frontage shall be landscaped. Kisco, New York (Section 80.25, Block 3, Lots 26 and 26.2) Dear Chairman McGuirk and Board Members: Our firm represents 175 Main St of Mount Kisco LLC, owner of the above-referenced property. The Board granted Site Plan Approval and a Change of Use Permit on March 26, 2024, and amended that approval on February 26, 2026. Copies of both resolutions are enclosed. The site work is substantially complete, and the second-floor residential units have been fully inspected and, subject to the Building Inspector’s confirmation, are ready for occupancy. Tenants are prepared to move in. We therefore seek the Board’s assistance with two limited outstanding matters. 1. Amendment of Condition #23 Condition #8 of the 2026 Resolution incorporates the conditions of the 2024 Resolution, including Condition #23, which prohibits issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy until all streetscape, off-site, and civic-space improvements are complete and approved by the Village Engineer. The required improvements are, or will be, substantially complete by the Board’s October 27 meeting. The sole remaining issue concerns the handicapped-accessibility requirements under Conditions #6 and #7 of the 2026 Resolution, potentially requiring a lift or elevator within approximately 100 square feet of the civic space. Resolution of this issue may take a few additional months. Chairman Michael McGuirk and Members of the Planning Board October 8, 2026 Page 2 We respectfully request that the Board amend Condition #23 to permit issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy upon “substantial completion” of the required improvements, notwithstanding the limited area remaining subject to resolution of the accessibility issue. Requiring absolute completion would unnecessarily delay occupancy of otherwise completed residential units. 2. Recommendation for a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy Village Code § 110-39E provides for Planning Board review of temporary Certificate of Occupancy applications, including an assessment of project completion and recommendations to the Building Inspector. See also 19 NYCRR § 1202.5. The application for a Certificate of Occupancy has been submitted. We respectfully request that the Board confirm the project’s substantial completion and recommend that the Building Inspector issue a temporary Certificate of Occupancy. The Board is welcome to inspect the property, and we would gladly arrange a site visit for any Board member. The building and residential units are complete and, subject to the Building Inspector’s confirmation, satisfy all applicable safety requirements. Required fire and life-safety systems are operational, and all required means of egress are provided. The only outstanding issue is the limited portion of the civic space affected by the unresolved accessibility question, which does not in any way impact safe state or local safety requirements for occupancy. Accordingly, we respectfully request that the Board amend Condition #23 to recognize substantial completion and recommend issuance of a temporary Certificate of Occupancy, allowing the completed residential units to be occupied while the limited remaining issue is resolved. We look forward to appearing before the Board on October 27 and appreciate its continued consideration. text: VILLAGE/TOWN OF MOUNT KISCO PROPOSED LOCAL LAW #03 OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO AMEND CHAPTER 96 – TAXATION OF THE CODE OF THE VILLAGE/TOWN OF MOUNT KISCO Be it enacted by the Village Board of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco of the County of Westchester as follows: Additions are reflected with Underlining, Deletions are reflected within Strikethrough Section 1. Legislative Intent. The Board of Trustees finds that the New York State Legislature has amended § 458-a of the Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) to authorize municipalities to adopt a full exemption from real property taxation for the primary residence of seriously disabled veterans meeting specified eligibility requirements. The Board further finds that the Village has long recognized the sacrifices made by veterans and their families. Consistent with that recognition, the Board desires to provide the fullest exemption authorized by law to those veterans whose service-connected disabilities have resulted in permanent and total disability. The Board also desires to increase the maximum exemption allowable for veterans, combat zone veterans, and disabled veterans under RPTL § 458-a for whom RPTL § 458-a. 11. does not apply The purpose of this Local Law is to amend Chapter 96 of the Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco to adopt the optional exemption authorized by RPTL § 458-a. 11., and to adopt a Veterans Alternative Exemption that will increase the maximum exemption allowable authorized by RPTL § 458-a. 2.(d)(ii). Section 2. Authority. This local law is adopted pursuant to Real Property Tax Law § 458-a. Section 3. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-16.3 Veterans; alternative tax exemption, as follows: § 96-16.3. Veterans; alternative tax exemption. A. Grant of exemption. Pursuant to § 458-a of the Real Property Tax Law (RPTL), qualifying residential real property as defined therein shall be eligible for the veterans alternative exemption as authorized therein. B. Maximum exemption amounts. The Village/Town of Mount Kisco hereby grants the following maximum exemption amounts as authorized by RPTL § 458-a: (1) War Veteran Exemption: $75,000 (2) Combat Veteran Exemption: $50,000. This exemption is in addition to any exemption granted under (1) of this subsection as authorized and permitted under RPTL § 458-a. (3) Disabled Veteran Exemption: $250,000 C. Seriously Disabled Veterans Exemption. Pursuant to RPTL § 458-a. 11., the Village/Town of Mount Kisco hereby grants the full real property tax exemption for seriously disabled veterans authorized therein. Section 4. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-17.3 Qualifications for veterans; alternative exemption. § 96-17.3. Qualifications for veterans; alternative exemption. Eligibility for the exemptions authorized by § 96-16.3 shall be determined in accordance with Real Property Tax Law (RPTL) § 458-a. No exemption as provided for in § 96-16.3 shall be granted unless all of the applicable qualifications and requirements of RPTL § 458-a are met. Section 5. The Code of the Village/Town of Mount Kisco Chapter 96 Taxation, Article III Real Property Tax Exemptions, is hereby amended to add a new § 96-18.3 Application for veterans; alternative exemption. § 96-18.3. text: TOWN OF NORTH ELBA LOCAL LAW __ OF 2026 ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS BE IT ENACTED BY THE NORTH ELBA TOWN BOARD AS FOLLOWS: 1. Title and Authority – This Local Law shall be known as the Town of North Elba Battery Energy Storage Systems Moratorium. It is adopted pursuant to Municipal Home Rule Law §10 and Town Law Article 16. 2. Purpose – The Town Board recognizes that Battery Energy Storage Systems facilities are a component to the promotion of renewable energy sources, however, the technology of these systems is still in its infancy. Public health, safety, and welfare are some of the highest priorities in the Town, causing the Town Board to want to have the ability to study the approach to and impacts from the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems facilities. This Moratorium is necessary in order to temporarily restrict the development of Battery Energy Storage Systems so that the Town Board may thoroughly consider the impacts of such uses, their appropriate locations in the community and how to allow for appropriate development of such facilities within the Town’s land use development and zoning objectives. The Town Board has determined that this would best enhance and protect the health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of North Elba. 3. Definitions – “Battery Energy Storage System” means one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy derived from any source including without limitation solar or wind sources, to be stored and then released at a future time. 4. Moratorium – The Town of North Elba hereby imposes a one-year Moratorium on the construction, establishment, installation, review or approval of any Battery Energy Storage Systems after the date that this Local Law takes effect. During the pendency of this Moratorium, there shall be no construction nor permits issued nor applications considered by the Town, its Officials, Boards or Departments for the construction, installation or use of Battery Energy Storage Systems. 5. Extensions – This Moratorium may be extended for such additional periods as the Town Board may determine to be necessary to protect the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the Town of North Elba and accomplish the stated purposes and intent of this Local Law. 6. Variance Procedure – The Town Board shall have the power, after a Public Hearing, to vary or modify the application of any provision of this Local Law upon its determination that strict application of this Local Law would impose extraordinary hardship upon an applicant and that the variance granted would not adversely affect the health, safety or welfare of the citizens of the Town or significantly conflict with the general purposes and intent of this Local Law. Any request for a variance shall be in writing and filed with the Town Clerk. The Town Board shall conduct a Public Hearing on the application on not less than five (5) days’ public notice and shall make its decision within thirty (30) days after the close of the Public Hearing. Any project which is granted a variance from this Local Law shall be subject to all requirements under the Town Code which would have been applicable to the project if the Moratorium had not been adopted and the prohibitions set forth in Paragraph 4 of this Local Law shall not apply to such project. 7. Severability – The invalidity of any clause, sentence, paragraph or provision of this Local Law shall not invalidate any other clause, sentence, paragraph or part thereof. 8. Effective Date – This Local Law shall take effect upon filing by the Office of the New York Secretary of State. TOWN OF NORTH ELBA NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING ON PROPOSED LOCAL LAW NO. __ OF 2026 ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON BATTERY ENERGY STORAGE SYSTEMS NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the North Elba Town Board will hold a Public Hearing on OCTOBER 13, 2026, beginning at 5:15 pm at the North Elba Town Hall, 2693 Main Street, Lake Placid, New York, concerning proposed Local Law No. __ of 2026. The proposed Local Law would establish a one-year moratorium on any Battery Energy Storage Systems facility in the Town of North Elba. title: Local Law # 5 of 2026
text: TOWN OF SALEM-COUNTY OF WASHINGTON LOCAL LAW #5 OF 2026 A LOCAL LAW TO OVERRIDE THE TAX LEVY LIMIT ESTABLISHED IN GENERAL MUNICIPAL LAW 3-c BE IT ENACTED by the Town Board of the Town of Salem, Washington County, New York, as follows: Section 1. Legislative Intent: It is the intent of this Local Law to override the limit on the amount of real property taxes that may be levied by the Town pursuant to General Municipal Law § 3-c, and to allow the Town of Salem to adopt a budget for the fiscal year beginning January 1, 2027 & ending December 31, 2027, that requires a real property tax levy in excess of the “tax levy limit” as defined by General Municipal Law § 3-c. Section 2. Authority: This Local Law is adopted pursuant to subdivision 5 of General Municipal Law § 3-c, which expressly authorizes the Town Board to override the tax levy limit by the adoption of a Local Law approved by vote of sixty percent (60%) of the town board. Section 3. Tax Levy Limit Override: The Town Board of the Town of Salem, County of Washington, is hereby authorized to adopt a budget for the fiscal year 2027 that requires a real property tax levy in excess of the amount otherwise prescribed in General Municipal Law, §3-c. Section 4. Severability: If any clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, or part of this Local Law or the application thereof to any person, firm or corporation, or circumstance, shall be adjusted by any court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or unconstitutional, such order or judgment shall not affect, impair, or invalidate the remainder thereof, but shall be confined in its operation to the clause, sentence, paragraph, subdivision, or part of this Local Law or in its application to the person, individual, firm or corporation or circumstance, directly involved in the controversy in which such judgment or order shall be rendered. Town Board Establishes a Zoning Commission The Town Board appoints a Zoning Commission to begin the process of developing zoning for the Town. If the Town already has a Planning Board, the Planning Board may be appointed to serve as the Zoning Commission. 2. Review the Town’s Comprehensive Plan and Community Goals The Zoning Commission reviews the Town’s existing Comprehensive Plan, planning documents, current land uses, community needs, and future goals. Zoning regulations must be developed in accordance with a comprehensive plan. 3. Gather Public Input The Zoning Commission should involve Town residents, property owners, businesses, and other interested parties throughout the process. Public informational meetings, surveys, workshops, and other methods may be used to determine what residents want zoning to accomplish. 4. Develop Proposed Zoning Districts The Zoning Commission identifies appropriate zoning districts for different areas of the Town. Examples could include: Residential Commercial Hamlet Rural Agricultural Industrial Mixed-use e Conservation or resource-protection areas eoeee#ee The appropriate districts would be determined based upon the characteristics and needs of the Town. 5. Prepare a Draft Zoning Map A proposed zoning map is developed showing the boundaries of each zoning district. 6. Prepare Draft Zoning Regulations The Zoning Commission develops proposed regulations explaining what types of uses and development would be permitted within each district. The regulations may address issues such as permitted uses, setbacks, building size, lot size, special uses, site plan review, and other land-use standards. 7. Zoning Commission Holds Public Hearing(s) The Zoning Commission prepares a preliminary proposal and holds one or more public hearings as appropriate to receive comments from the public. The proposal may be revised based upon the comments received. 8. Zoning Commission Submits Final Report After completing its work, the Zoning Commission prepares and submits its final recommendations, proposed zoning regulations, and zoning map to the Town Board. The Town Board must receive the Zoning Commission’s final report before the Town Board holds its own public hearing or takes action on the proposed zoning. 9. Complete Required Reviews and Referrals Before adoption, the Town must complete applicable legal reviews, including: e State Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) review; e Referral to the County Planning Agency when required under General Municipal Law §239-m; e Required notices to neighboring municipalities and other governmental entities when applicable; and e Review by the Town Attorney. 10. Town Board Holds a Public Hearing The Town Board holds a formal public hearing on the proposed zoning regulations and zoning map. Notice of the Town Board’s zoning public hearing must be published at least 10 days before the hearing. Residents and other interested parties are given an opportunity to comment. 11. Town Board Considers Adoption Following the public hearing and completion of all required reviews, the Town Board considers whether to adopt the proposed zoning regulations and zoning map. The Board may make appropriate changes before adoption, subject to applicable legal requirements. 12. Publication, Filing and Effective Date After adoption, the zoning law or ordinance must be properly entered into the Town’s records, published and filed as required by New York law. The Town Clerk maintains the official zoning law and zoning map. 13. Establish the Zoning Administration Process Once zoning is adopted, the Town must establish procedures for administering and enforcing it. This may include: Designating a Zoning Enforcement Officer; Establishing or designating a Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA); Establishing permit and application procedures; Establishing procedures for variances, interpretations and appeals; and Coordinating zoning review with the Planning Board, Code Enforcement Officer and Town Board. If that is the Town's policy, there should be clear legal authority establishing it and evidence that the same standard is being applied consistently to similarly situated commercial properties. If comparable commercial properties are being assessed differently, the Town should be able to identify the objective distinctions that justify those differences.
